holes.name: Banner Drive
holes.narrative: Where the adventure begins… Formally elevated pallet tee box. Lots of festivity behind you. Lots of potential glory in front of you. Relatively flat fairway. Slightly breaks left. Need to be wary of the actual banner streaking diagonally across. Can be a difficult range to calibrate to off the bat with pre-round nerves. A fairly long distance to pin but very easy, especially with the dry October conditions, to blow by it. You're off n runnin!

holes.name: Dick Basket
holes.narrative: The lovable enigma. The Dick Basket. Any asshole can throw a dick at a basket. But can he get it to STICK??? So many approach angle options, but everyone's got a strategy until they get hit in the face with a DICK. Despite all of the above, this is still a fan favorite! Nothing captures the drama and suspense of the BBGC better than a ball teetering on the rim of the DB. Enjoy

holes.name: Slippery Slope
holes.narrative: Okay, again, I ask for your understanding and grace with the imperfections of this course this year after having multiple tractors and semi-trucks drive through and rip up my lawn in the process of tearing out our septic tank earlier this summer. Slippery Slope is one of the fairways impacted, at least visually, as your target landing zone wouldn't likely be before the tire treads anyway. As the name implies, this one gets SLICK, especially as the day progresses and the track gets smoothed out. One of the longer drives, but because it's downhill, muscle isn't the requirement, touch is.

holes.name: Ol Smokey
holes.narrative: A pin placement at the top of the back ridge. It will have back bumpers that will be relatively close to the pin that will be designed to be bouncy, so hitting it will endanger your ball to head back down the slope. It will also be pretty close to the base of the tree, which will be very much in play on many shots.

holes.name: Up N At Em
holes.narrative: We serve Spunky Dunker Donuts and McD's breakfast sammies so you'll have the strength to drive this uphill beast. Due to the aforementioned septic truck tire treads, if you overshoot the green this year, those tread tracks serve as an escape hatch sending your ball back to you. There are rails along the right and back side of the fairway to play off of, but not advised. The best fairway at golden hour. Soak it in.

holes.name: Bump N Run
holes.narrative: A PHYSICAL par 3. Early shots need touch to avoid the stump gates and nestle by the pin, but second shots can get outright violent to knock balls off/near the flag. We added border logs in the rough off both sides of the green to make ball collection of errant throws easier.

holes.name: The Vice
holes.narrative: Gets its name from the V-shaped fairway. You can play the slope either way. Most play right to left, but you can get caught up there, or, more often, come down from right slope with too much speed and overshoot pin. The central “valley floor” of it can play really fast with drier conditions. A little tricky to gauge speed as it starts uphill but finishes w a downslope. Bottom of the pin is blind from the tee box so it gets dramatic to find out where shots wind up after all balls thrown. There is more of a backstop with an expanded flower garden bed around the electrical boxes but that area is barely within 10'.

holes.name: Heartbreak Ridge
holes.narrative: As the name implies, you can have a nice soft approach, but it will break your heart if it doesn't end with a release down the hard dogleg left slope to the pin. Some put balls there intentionally for defensive purposes. In recent years with more branch clearing above, some have gone the over plop route. Others, even more recently, have attempted to approach from the left, using the tree mound BEHIND the pin….if you're a back door man.

holes.name: The Island
holes.narrative: Yes, we have moved The Island tee box about 20ft to the left. This was done for two reasons; first of all, it eliminates the tight proximity the former tee box had with Heartbreak Ridge's green. There were some close calls of guys standing within 10ft of that pin in the queue to drive 9 and interfering with live balls. Secondly, it provides a longer landing runway AND a fun backstop. Visually more attractive as well.

holes.name: Lagoni Lane
holes.narrative: High profile hole being along the driveway and the turn. Lots of spectators can add pressure. MUCH drier than previous years (we found out our neighbors' irrigation line had a crack in it), however, it can get sticky quick depending on how much precip we get tomorrow. With a little rain, this hole is a treat for the bocce purists as you rarely see a BFB here. Tosses are generally true. Flick n STICK.

holes.name: South Hill Sling
holes.narrative: Down into the heart of the back 9 we dive!!! This one invites the rain tomorrow, as not having much in last three weeks has this one playing FAST. Can be a major advantage to have a lefty partner on this one, otherwise, play the left breaking hill to the pin. Or you can go straight up and over through the silver maple as we did major pruning on it this past offseason.

holes.name: The Playpen
holes.narrative: We moved the pin closer to the tee box by a few feet last year to prevent “side of the barn” crutch shots. You can still play it off the side of the play set and be within scoring range, but it won't be right on the pin as it was before. Note: the back rail has multiple crevices, only one of them is the one where the pin lays.

holes.name: South Mouth
holes.narrative: This somma bitch….he's a little closer to tee box this year. The main reason for that is we wanted to incentivize more attempts into his mouth, but it's also because SouthMouth wants to be closer to “where his friends hangout”, so he can feel included. We also moved him a little further into the lawn to open up the right fairway to play some more. There are logs approaching the green that will angle balls towards the pin if struck. There is now a bell mounted to the playpen. If you get a throw successfully into SM's mouth, ring the bell. If you hear the bell on the course, let out your best gargle roar. This is fun

holes.name: Rustlers Gambit Windmill
holes.narrative: Well you're standing on ground zero of 'The Great Septic Tank Rip Out of 2025' here. The dirt mound is tarp-covered for your protection, but the hole still plays the same….either run the gamut through the windmill-topped tunnel, or plop a shot over it. We added a water-hazard to it this year just past the tunnel on the left side of the fairway.

holes.name: Border Creek Rock
holes.narrative: I highly recommend slowing down to enjoy the nature trail that leads you from 14 to this tree-canopied cozy tee box along the namesake border creek. You'll need to save your strength for this Par 5. Note: the septic tank replacement trucks really created deep tire grooves impacting this fairway. It's a little bumpy, but still plays the same. You can use the back hill or flagstone back stop….or….

holes.name: Cancelled Cliffs of Latrell
holes.narrative: You love it or hate it. Extremely low margin for error hole. New stumps line the small green. They're slightly narrower than before. If you don't make it onto the green, you're likely rolling down the hill. If you hit it too hard, you can go straight through it out the back tunnel.

holes.name: Fairway to Heaven
holes.narrative: So many pressure-cooked shots have been thrown here. Do you head up the stairs to 18 protecting a lead? Charging from behind? Falling apart? Keep it together man.

holes.name: Bombs Over Barrington
holes.narrative: Voted Sexiest Elevated Tee Box by Bocce Golf Magazine NINE CONSECUTIVE YEARS. This is what it often comes down to! Reminder: the water hazard on this hole is minus a point.
